findings: Document inconsistency in definition of 'Business Day'. In document 1, 'Business Day' means Monday to Friday. In document 2 and 4, 'Business Day' means Monday to Saturday. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:1.2 & 02_sow.md:1.1

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Schedule'. In document 1, 'Schedule' refers to documents executed by both parties and expressly stated as a Schedule. In document 3, 'Schedule' is referenced without being explicitly defined. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:1.4 & 03_dpa.md:5.2

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Incident'. In document 1, 'Incident' means unplanned interruption or reduction of quality of Services. In documents 3 and 4, 'Incident' is not defined but used without being clearly understood. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:1.2 & 03_dpa.md:1.2

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Subprocessor'. In document 1, Subprocessor means any third party engaged by Provider to process Customer Personal Data. In document 3, it's stated that all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information and thus no Subprocessors are permitted without explicit consent. This creates a conflict. 01_dpa.md:5.2 & 03_dpa.md:5.1

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Maintenance Window'. In document 4, it's stated that Provider shall give not less than five (5) Business Days' notice of a maintenance window. However, in document 1, 'Business Day' is defined as Monday to Friday. This creates a conflict regarding the calculation of days. 03_sla.md:3.4 & 01_msa.md:1.2

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Availability'. In document 3, it's stated that Provider shall achieve monthly availability of the platform of not less than 99.9%. However, in document 4, Availability is calculated differently (total minutes in the month less unavailable minutes) divided by total minutes in the month. This creates a conflict. 03_sla.md:3.1 & 04_sla.md:3.2

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Security Incident'. In document 1, it's stated that Provider shall notify Customer of any Security Incident without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it. This is then referenced as a Priority 1 incident. In document 3, this is defined differently from being treated as a Priority 1 incident. 01_dpa.md:6.1 & 03_dpa.md:7.1

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Resolution'. In documents 1 and 4, Resolution means the restoration of the Services to normal operation. However, in document 5 (Service Level and Support Schedule), it's stated that Resolution refers to response within a certain timeframe followed by action within another timeframe. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:13.2 & 04_sla.md:5.3

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Support Hours'. In document 1, Support is available twenty-four hours a day and every day. In documents 3 and 4, there are specific times (8:00-18:00) specified. This creates a conflict as it's unclear which version applies. 01_msa.md:2.1 & 03_sla.md:2.1

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Response Time'. In document 4, Response times are measured from the point at which Provider acknowledges an Incident. However, there is no acknowledgment process defined in documents 1 and 2. This creates a conflict. 04_sla.md:5.1 & 01_msa.md:6.1

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Maintenance Window'. In document 4, it's stated that Provider shall give not less than five (5) Business Days' notice of a maintenance window. However, there is no mention of this requirement in documents 3 and 2. This creates a conflict. 04_sla.md:3.4 & 02_sow.md:4.2

Document inconsistency in term definition for 'Agreed Maintenance Window'. In document 1, Agreed maintenance windows are excluded from the calculation of Availability. However, there is no mention of this exclusion in documents 3 and 2. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:3.3 & 03_sla.md:3.4

Document inconsistency regarding 'Security Incident' response time. In document 3, Provider shall notify Customer's nominated security contact of a Security Incident within seventy-two (72) hours of confirming it. However, there is no mention of this requirement in documents 1 and 4. This creates a conflict. 03_dpa.md:6.1 & 04_sla.md:7.1

Document inconsistency regarding 'Service Level'. In document 1, Service level is defined as availability of not less than 99.5%. However, in document 3, it's stated that service levels are to be achieved from the start of Phase 3 onwards with a minimum of 99.9% availability. This creates a conflict. 01_msa.md:7.2 & 03_dpa.md:3.5

findings: The term 'Deliverable' in document 1 (MSA) is defined differently from what is stated in Document 2 (SOW). In the MSA, Deliverables are identified as items in a Statement of Work, whereas SOW defines them as items delivered by Provider. This definition inconsistency could lead to confusion. Document 1 (MSA), Section 1.4

Document 3 (DPA) mentions that Provider shall notify Customer of Security Incidents 'without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it.' However, Document 4 (SLA) defines a Security Incident as an 'unconfirmed' incident. There is no definition of 'unconfirmed' provided, which could lead to ambiguity. Document 3 (DPA), Section 6.1 and Document 4 (SLA), Section 7.2

Document 1 (MSA), Section 2.1 and Document 4 (SLA), throughout the document
